rules.statement: Write interface inputs i_wr_en, i_wr_data and the software reset i_rst_n_sw change only at a rising edge of i_clk_wr.
Read interface input i_rd_en changes only at a rising edge of i_clk_rd.
Hardware resets are asserted and released at a rising edge of their own clock.

rules.condition: In the cycle in which i_rst_n_sw falls to 0
rules.statement: Writes are blocked with zero latency: i_wr_en is not accepted, o_full = 1 and o_full_thr takes the empty-FIFO value 0.

rules.condition: From the write FSM leaving RUN (event 2) until the write FSM returns to RUN (event 13)
rules.statement: o_sw_rst_busy is 1 from the write FSM leaving RUN until it returns to RUN.

rules.condition: During the software reset sequence until the write release
rules.statement: Writes stay blocked throughout the sequence, including after i_rst_n_sw is released; the write pointer does not move and storage is not written.

rules.condition: When the reset request becomes visible in the read domain
rules.statement: Reads are blocked: i_rd_en is not accepted, o_empty = 1 and o_empty_thr = 1 in the same cycle.

rules.condition: Before the request is visible in the read domain
rules.statement: Reads accepted before the request reaches the read domain are normal reads returning valid pre-reset words.

rules.condition: During the software reset handshake
rules.statement: The read pointer is reset before ack_rd rises.

rules.condition: During the software reset handshake
rules.statement: The write pointer is reset only after the acknowledge is seen in the write domain.

rules.condition: After the write pointer is reset
rules.statement: The write FSM waits in HOLD for i_rst_n_sw = 1, and passes HOLD without waiting if the input is already 1.

rules.condition: After i_rst_n_sw is released
rules.statement: The write FSM drops the request req_wr to 0 after release of i_rst_n_sw.

rules.condition: At release
rules.statement: The read side is released first (ack_rd = 0, flags live, o_empty = 1) and the write side last, because write release needs ack_rd = 0.

rules.condition: When the write FSM returns to RUN
rules.statement: Writes are unblocked, o_full = 0, o_full_thr is normal and o_sw_rst_busy = 0.

rules.condition: After the sequence
rules.statement: The first write after the reset is accepted; o_empty and o_empty_thr fall only after the write pointer has crossed to the read domain.

rules.condition: While writes are blocked by the software reset
rules.statement: o_overflow does not pulse for a blocked write access.

rules.condition: After read release with empty FIFO and i_rd_en = 1
rules.statement: A read request on an empty FIFO after the read release is not blocked and o_underflow pulses once.

rules.condition: FIFO full, no reset, and producer keeps writing
rules.statement: o_overflow pulses, registered one cycle after the rejected write request.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw low for only one write-clock cycle
rules.statement: The write FSM latches the request at the first write edge, so a one-cycle low pulse on i_rst_n_sw completes the full sequence.

rules.condition: During the whole software reset on a full FIFO
rules.statement: o_full stays 1 during the whole reset and falls at the write release; o_full_thr follows the empty-FIFO value while blocked.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw is 0, including when the write FSM is in REL or reaches RUN
rules.statement: Writes are blocked whenever i_rst_n_sw is 0, including in REL and the cycle reaching RUN; no write is accepted between sequences.

rules.condition: i_rst_n_sw asserted again while write FSM is in REL
rules.statement: A second sequence starts at once after the first and completes the same way; o_sw_rst_busy falls for one write-clock cycle between them while o_full stays 1.

rules.condition: Hardware reset asserted during the software reset sequence
rules.statement: Both FSMs, both pointers and both request and acknowledge synchronizers go to reset values at once, whatever the handshake state (hardware reset priority).

rules.condition: After hardware reset release
rules.statement: After release the FIFO is empty (o_empty = 1, o_full = 0, pointers 0, FSMs in RUN) and works normally.

rules.condition: During hardware reset until both domains are out of reset
rules.statement: The testbench keeps traffic idle until both domains are out of reset.
